# Para

> Para is an open-source, stateless and schemaless backend with a REST API over any database, search index and cache. Self-host it anywhere, or let Para Cloud run it for you.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](/docs/index.md): Para is a stateless, schemaless backend with a REST API over pluggable persistence, search, and cache layers. Start with the quickstart, then open the topic you need.
- [Quickstart](/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Para is a flexible backend service, created as an open-source project from the very beginning, in 2013. It was born out of our need to have a robust system which would allow us…

- [Environment profiles](/docs/configuration/environments.md): para.env is an important configuration property that turns features on and off. There are two main values for it - development, production, but you can define more.

- [Serialization](/docs/concepts/serialization.md): Para handles serialization and deserialization using a combination of Jackson, BeanUtils and Java reflection. The process happens in the ParaObjectUtils class, and more…
- [User-defined classes](/docs/concepts/user-defined-types.md): Let's say you have a class Article in your application that you wish to persist. You first implement the ParaObject interface, then add a few data fields to it. Implementing…
- [Apps](/docs/concepts/apps.md): Apps allow you to have separate namespaces and data models for different purposes. Each app lives in its own separate database table and is independent from apps.

- [Generic SQL](/docs/data-stores/sql.md): Besides the default H2 implementation, there's a generic SQL DAO plugin which adds support for all the major RDBMS - MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle and…
- [H2 DB](/docs/data-stores/h2.md): This is the default database for object storage since v1.25. It is lightweight and embedded, which speeds up the startup of the server. All tables are stored inside a ./data…
- [Search interface](/docs/search/search-interface.md): Para indexes objects based on their type. For example, a User objects has a type field with the value "user". Most of the search methods below ask for a type to search for…
- [Elasticsearch](/docs/search/elasticsearch.md): Now part of the para-search-elasticsearch plugin.
- [Lucene](/docs/search/lucene.md): Lucene is used as the default search engine in Para. It is a lightweight alternative to Elasticsearch for self-contained deployments. It works great for local development and…
- [Cache interface](/docs/cache/cache-interface.md): The Cache interface defines the following methods used for object caching:
- [Caffeine](/docs/cache/caffeine.md): Caffeine is the default cache implementation since v1.26. It's built on top of the excellent Caffeine library by Ben Manes. This cache supports automatic eviction and TTL for…
- [Hazelcast](/docs/cache/hazelcast.md): Hazelcast allows you to use a portion of the memory on each node for caching without having to manage a separate caching server or cluster. Hazelcast was the default…
- [One-to-many relationships](/docs/concepts/one-to-many.md): Object relationships are defined by the Linkable interface. All Para objects are linkable, meaning that they can be related to other Para objects.
- [Many-to-many relationships](/docs/concepts/many-to-many.md): Many-to-many relationships are implemented in Para with Linker objects. This object contains information about a link between two objects. This is simply the id and type of…
- [Collecting metrics](/docs/operations/observability/overview.md): With version 1.27, a number of metrics are implemented on top of DropWizard. By default, DropWizard metrics are captured for every application, as well as the overall system…
- [Health check](/docs/operations/observability/health.md): A simple health check is mapped to /v1/health which returns 200 OK if the server is "healthy", and 500 if it's "unhealthy". The health check is configured to simply read the…
- [Logging](/docs/operations/observability/logging.md): Para uses SLF4J as a logging abstraction framework, meaning you can plug in any logging implementation like Logback, Log4j2, etc. By default Para uses Logback. To use another…
- [Translations](/docs/operations/i18n/translations.md): Translations are Para objects which contain a single translation of a string. For example you can have a language file in English and for each string you can create a…
- [Languages](/docs/operations/i18n/languages.md): Languages are maps of keys and values. A language file might contain all strings used by an application. Also you can have the language loaded from a database.
- [Filters](/docs/integrations/filters.md): There are several filters you can use to enable different features like Gzip encoding, CORS, etc.
- [Misc. utilities](/docs/utilities/overview.md): The Utils static class contains a variety of utility methods. These are summarized below:
- [HumanTime](/docs/utilities/human-time.md): Para includes the class HumanTime written by Johann Burkard. This class makes it easy to convert a timestamp to an approximation in the form of "X minutes ago".
